options.title: Learn more about bed availability issues
options.description: Collect data on the frequency and duration of high bed occupancy and long room-to-physician times. Identify the root causes of these issues and their potential impact on patient care and staff well-being.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If bed availability issues are found to be systemic, pressure may shift to the administration for resource allocation and planning.
options.how_we_would_know: Regular reports on bed occupancy, room-to-physician times, and patient wait times will provide insight into the frequency and severity of the issues.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the issues are found to be sporadic or within acceptable thresholds, no further action may be required. However, if the issues are persistent and impacting patient care, further steps should be taken.

options.title: Implement reserve monitored beds
options.description: Designate a certain number of monitored beds as reserves for acute arrivals. These beds should be made available for CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients, ensuring immediate access to monitored care upon arrival.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure may shift to the administration for resource allocation and to the nursing staff for bed management and patient flow.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitoring bed occupancy and the number of CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients with immediate access to monitored beds will indicate the effectiveness of this measure.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the reserve monitored bed system leads to improved access for critical patients, it should be continued. If not, further adjustments may be necessary.

options.title: Adjust rooming pace
options.description: Match the pace of rooming patients to the capacity of available clinicians. This may involve adjusting the pace of rooming to ensure that clinicians can keep up with the demand, reducing wait times.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure may shift to the nursing staff for effective patient flow management and to the administration for resource allocation to support the adjusted rooming pace.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitoring rooming pace, physician capacity, and wait times will indicate the success of this adjustment.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the adjusted rooming pace leads to reduced wait times and improved patient flow, it should be continued. If not, further adjustments may be necessary.

recommendation.rationale: Given the low strength of available evidence, it is recommended to first learn more about the issues and their potential impact. This will provide a more comprehensive understanding of the situation before implementing any process adjustments.
recommendation.would_change_if: If the issues are found to be more frequent or severe than anticipated, or if the initial data collection reveals clear root causes and solutions, the recommendation may shift towards more immediate process adjustments.

suggested_reviewers.why: The Nurse Manager is responsible for overseeing nursing operations and can provide valuable insights into the issues and potential solutions.
The Physician Lead can offer insights into physician capacity and potential solutions to reduce wait times.
The Administration is responsible for resource allocation and can provide support and guidance for implementing any recommended changes.

options.title: Protect reserve monitored beds
options.description: Implement a process to protect a small number of monitored beds for acute arrivals, ensuring immediate access to monitored beds.
options.local_fit: This option aligns with the policy expectation of immediate access to monitored beds for CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients. However, it may be challenging to implement in a context of high bed occupancy and extended room-to-physician times.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure may shift to the charge nurse and physician lead to ensure the protected beds are available when needed. They will need to carefully manage bed allocation and patient flow.
options.how_we_would_know: We can track the success of this option by monitoring the availability of monitored beds for acute arrivals and the overall patient flow through the emergency department.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the protected bed strategy fails to improve patient flow and satisfaction, or if it leads to increased wait times for other patient categories.

options.title: Trigger escalation huddles
options.description: Implement escalation huddles triggered by room-to-physician wait-time thresholds to address potential delays and improve patient flow.
options.local_fit: This option can help address extended room-to-physician times and potential patient flow issues. However, the effectiveness may be limited by the high bed occupancy and the potential surge in patient arrivals.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure may shift to the charge nurse and physician lead to manage the escalation process and ensure timely patient care. They will need to coordinate with other departments to create capacity.
options.how_we_would_know: We can evaluate the success of this option by tracking the frequency and effectiveness of escalation huddles, as well as the impact on room-to-physician times and patient flow.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the escalation huddles do not lead to significant improvements in room-to-physician times or patient flow, or if they become a regular occurrence, indicating a systemic issue.

options.title: Match rooming pace to capacity
options.description: Monitor and adjust the rooming pace to match the capacity of clinicians, especially during periods of high bed occupancy and potential patient surges.
options.local_fit: This option can help prevent rooming from continuing while the physician pace slows, which may contribute to extended room-to-physician times. However, it may be challenging to implement in a context of high bed occupancy and potential patient surges.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure may shift to the charge nurse and physician lead to ensure that rooming pace is appropriately adjusted. They will need to closely monitor clinician capacity and make real-time adjustments.
options.how_we_would_know: We can assess the effectiveness of this option by tracking the alignment between rooming pace and clinician capacity, as well as the impact on room-to-physician times and patient flow.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the adjustment of rooming pace fails to improve room-to-physician times or patient flow, or if it leads to increased wait times for other patient categories.

recommendation.rationale: The leading option, 'Protect reserve monitored beds', has the potential to directly address the policy gap by ensuring immediate access to monitored beds for acute arrivals. While the evidence strength is low, this option has a strong local fit as it aligns with the policy expectation and can be implemented relatively quickly. The other options, while potentially beneficial, may face challenges due to the high bed occupancy and extended room-to-physician times.
recommendation.would_change_if: If additional evidence suggests that the high bed occupancy is a result of systematic issues or if the extended room-to-physician times are primarily due to factors beyond the control of the physicians, the leading option may need to be re-evaluated.

suggested_reviewers.why: They can provide insights into the current challenges and potential solutions, especially regarding patient flow and bed management.
Their expertise can help assess the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed options, especially regarding physician capacity and workload.
